arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ayestas's lawyer argued the law entitles indigent inmates to reasonably necessary services.
The lawyer defined necessary services as those a reasonable attorney would use.
The lawyer noted the original mitigation presentation lasted only two minutes.
The state's lawyer argued the claim lacks jurisdiction under federal law.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Manuel Ayestas faces execution in Texas. He wants federal money to hire experts. The state denies this request. The case tests the scope of federal funding laws.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the financial resources available to death row inmates. It determines whether federal courts must fund extensive expert investigations. The outcome shapes the practical ability of defendants to challenge their sentences.
